slides.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning and Modern Game Search
slides.visibleText:
DRIVING QUESTION
When is a branch irrelevant?

Minimax gives the decision rule. Alpha-beta adds path bounds that let a depth-first search stop evaluating branches that cannot change the backed-up choice.

RESULT
Same minimax action
At the same depth and with the same evaluation function.
MECHANISM
α and β bounds
They summarize already established alternatives on the active path.
EFFICIENCY
Order matters
Good moves first can expose cutoffs earlier.
EVIDENCE
Trace every return
A cutoff must follow from a bound, not intuition.

slides.title: Minimax may pursue branches whose values cannot matter
slides.visibleText:
SEARCH PROBLEM
The game tree grows faster than the search budget

Full depth-limited minimax evaluates every reachable leaf to its ply limit—even after an ancestor has a demonstrably better alternative.

ALPHA-BETA PROMISE

Return the same minimax value and action at the same search depth.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE

Terminal utility, cutoff depth, and evaluation function remain the same.

WHAT DOES CHANGE

Depth-first visitation and move ordering expose bounds that skip remaining siblings.

STRUCTURAL INSIGHT
A value found below ply n+1 can establish a relation between the decision at ply n and a descendant at ply n+2, proving the entire intervening subtree irrelevant.

slides.title: Alpha rises for MAX; beta falls for MIN
slides.visibleText:
ACTIVE INTERVAL
α ≤ possible backed-up value ≤ β

The interval records what the ancestors already know. Once the lower bound meets or exceeds the upper bound, the remaining siblings cannot affect the ancestor’s choice.

ALPHA · LOWER BOUND

The best value MAX can already guarantee along the current path.

BETA · UPPER BOUND

The best value MIN can already guarantee along the current path.

MONOTONICITY

α never decreases; β never increases as the active path is searched.

CUTOFF CONDITION
The interval closes when α≥β, equivalently β≤α.

slides.title: A cutoff says an ancestor already has a better alternative
slides.visibleText:
AT A MAX NODE
v ≥ β

Stop evaluating its remaining children. An ancestor MIN node can force an outcome no larger than β.

STANDARD NAME
Beta cutoff

The MAX node reached or exceeded the MIN ancestor’s upper bound.

AT A MIN NODE
v ≤ α

This is an alpha cutoff. An ancestor MAX node already guarantees at least α elsewhere.

slides.title: Alpha and beta summarize alternatives outside the current subtree
slides.visibleText:
PATH MEMORY
[α, β] is a decision-relevant window

Bounds are not predictions and not prefilters. They become valid only from values already returned by completed search.

Α · MAX’S FLOOR

A MAX ancestor can obtain at least α through an explored alternative.

Β · MIN’S CEILING

A MIN ancestor can hold MAX to at most β through an explored alternative.

V · CURRENT EVIDENCE

The temporary value at this node after one or more child returns.

DO NOT PREFILTER
Examine children in order until a returned value proves α≥β. “Only examine values above α or below β” is not a valid rule.

QUESTION
BEST-FIRST ORDERING
WORST-FIRST ORDERING
INVARIANT
MAX TRIES

High-value moves early

Low-value moves early

Same legal actions

MIN TRIES

Low-value moves early

High-value moves early

Same cutoff depth

EFFECT

Tight bounds and earlier cutoffs

Few cutoffs; near-full minimax

Same evaluation function

RESULT

More leaves evaluated

Same minimax result

Root MAX has α=3. Its next MIN child sees leaves 8 and 10. After seeing 8, is there an alpha cutoff?

A

B

slides.title: Ordering reduces evaluations; other game models change the backup rule
slides.visibleText:
1
Poor ordering

Few early bounds; alpha-beta approaches full minimax work.

2
Good ordering

Likely strong MAX moves and weak MIN moves first; more cutoffs occur early.

3
Correctness

Either order returns the same depth-limited minimax result.

4
Measurement

Record evaluated leaves, internal nodes, time, and ordering overhead.

MODERN SUPPLEMENTS

Expectimax: chance nodes back up probability-weighted expected utility when outcomes are stochastic.

Monte Carlo Tree Search: selectively grows a tree using repeated selection, expansion, simulation, and backup.

These alter the game-search model; they are not alpha-beta shortcuts for deterministic minimax.
